Dualtron's Rovoron R7 Pro E-Scooter Is Their Flagship Adventure Model – Aimed at All Terrains
8 photos
Photo: Dualtron USA
The ages have been good from a speed-loving vehicle standpoint, with decade after decade yielding faster cars, motorcycles, water toys, airplanes, you name it. Even bicycles didn’t escape the grip of “faster!” Yet, there’s one vehicle in particular that may have gone too far. That vehicle is the e-scooter.
Let’s face it, back in my day, about 25-30 years ago, the kick-scooter was considered a toy. As I aged, I saw that some of my friends we’re pimping out specialized platforms with, what is essentially , a chainsaw motor, solid suspension, brakes, and then ripping it up around the neighborhood with a modified exhaust that could be heard coming blocks away.
Photo: Dualtron Fast forward a few years, and the electrification of our world would take place, and the scooters of old would not be exempt from the equation, yielding monstrous machines that are even able to top speeds some cars would never dream of touching. Some e-scooters clear 100 mph easy and that’s actually what they were designed for.
Would you ride such a beast? Drop a comment below.
This electric boom also sparked countless brands that are responsible for e-scooters that can touch break-neck speeds. Those are pretty niche brands and not everyone would be comfortable climbing on an e-scooter that can reach highway speeds.
Some brands, however, are a bit more reserved , going as far as also supplying the market with e-scooters that are a bit more “humble,” so to speak. One such team is Dualtron. Yet, don’t be mistaken; while our centerpiece of discussion today is an e-scooter from this brand that only tops out at 40 mph (64 kph), Dualtron is known for bringing some monsters to the market, the kind that really can keep up with your car.
Photo: Dualtron The Rovoron R7 Pro, on the other hand, is an e-scooter that’s designed to offer a bit less speed than the average Dualtron machine, and it does so with a purpose: this e-scooter is the brand’s flagship Adventure e-scooter, designed to handle roads with or without tarmac, maybe even a trail or two judging by the customizable spring-driven C-arm suspension at the front.
Ample ground clearance is also an indicator that this EV is designed for roads with obstacles, if the rugged frame wasn’t enough to suggest the same. The 11-inch self-healing pneumatic tires are also a solid component to have.
Now, at the heart of the R7 Pro are not one, but two motors, one for each wheel, offering a combined output of 1,800 W. This, however, is a nominal output, and after I consulted the R7 handbook, which does mention that 900 W per motor is the nominal strength, I also found a little section that mentions a peak of 3.3 kW (4.4 hp). The entire ecosystem is tuned to operate on 60 V, so there’s clearly some punchy acceleration too.
What I had a hard time finding was just how steep of a hill this two-wheeler can handle, and
Dualtron, if you’re reading this, drop a comment below. Better yet, drop an e-mail.
Photo: Dualtron In terms of range, the R7 Pro is said to be suitable for up to 55 miles (88.5 km manufacturer-reported), made possible by a massive 42.2 Ah battery. While the real world is bound to yield a different number, even pulling in 30 miles with both motors active is a number that I find appealing .
If you’re riding around off-road, the chances that you’ll be blasting around at full speed are much lower than on tarmac, but what will affect your range out there are all the inclines and rough terrain the motors encounter. Once drained, it can take a bit over six hours to be back on your feet, with the use of a fast charger.
While speed isn’t everything off-road, handling is, and aside from the suspension, a system which I’ve tested on multiple e-scooters over the years, the Pro is rocking a set of Nutt hydraulic clampers with ABS and EBS to help control traction to come to a safe stop.
Photo: Dualtron The weight of this trinket is also an aid in helping us stay stable off the tarmac, with a standard unit rolling in at 105 lbs (48 kg), enough to keep you planted while making your way to grandma’s house in the woods. What this weight won’t help in is making it up a flight or two of stairs, even though the frame is a foldable one. You’ll need to hit up the gym for this one.
Toss on some lighting, including turn signals, finger-pull throttle, and the new EY3 display, a compact little hub that let’s you keep an eye on speed and a few other parameters, and we have the Rovoron R7 Pro.
That leaves us with the one and only other topic of discussion: Price. Whether it’s because of Black Friday or Dualtron is just in a giving mood, but the Rovoron R7 Pro is currently up for grabs at $2,000, a $400 price drop.
If that’s too much for you, keep in mind that you can still find a standard R7 in select dealers, even though Dualtron’s USA website no longer advertises it. Some dealers are selling this one for $1,200, but there are some clear downgrades you’ll need to support. Ride safe out there; gear up properly.

Borderlands Mexico is a weekly rundown of developments in the world of United States-Mexico cross-border trucking and trade. This week in Borderlands Mexico: Truckers secure 29 agreements on highway safety after nationwide strike; MISUMI Americas expands Mexico operations with new 45,000-square-foot facility; and Prime Fuel Solutions expands Texas fleet, targets neighboring states.
Truckers secure 29 agreements on highway safety after nationwide strike
Mexico’s federal government and trucking industry representatives have advanced 29 agreements aimed at combating cargo theft, improving highway security and addressing deteriorating infrastructure.
The agreements arrive nearly a month after nationwide trucker protests disrupted freight transportation across 19 states.
The deals emerged from six working groups involving 10 government authorities and representatives of the National Chamber of Freight Transportation (CANACAR), the Honorable Mexican Alliance of Transport Organizations (HAMOTAC), the Mexican-American Federation of Transporters (FEMATRAC) and the Integrating Organization of Conventional Rights (INDECO).
The organizations, supported by Mexico’s Confederation of National Chambers of Commerce, Services and Tourism (CONCANACO SERVYTUR), announced the progress Wednesday, during a news conference in Mexico City.
The negotiations focus on persistent problems affecting Mexico’s trucking industry, including cargo theft, extortion, highway maintenance, excessive towing charges, regulatory requirements and the safety of commercial truck drivers.
The discussions follow an Oct. 26-27 nationwide trucking strike that prompted demonstrations and highway blockades across major freight corridors.
Mexico’s Interior Ministry reported demonstrations at 38 locations across 19 states, involving 691 vehicles and 858 participants.
The protests highlighted concerns about highway crime and rising transportation costs, particularly along routes connecting Mexico’s industrial centers to U.S. border crossings.
Highway security and cargo theft remain top priorities
One of the central components of the negotiations involves improving coordination among Mexico’s Interior Ministry (SEGOB), the Ministry of Security and Citizen Protection (SSPC), the National Guard and state authorities.
The agreements call for establishing direct communication channels between transportation companies and law enforcement agencies to report criminal activity and respond to security incidents.
Authorities and trucking representatives also agreed to work toward standardizing procedures used by prosecutors, including efforts to accelerate the release of recovered trucks following cargo theft investigations.
Other measures include identifying unauthorized highway checkpoints and strengthening enforcement against devices used to jam GPS tracking signals.
The initiatives are intended to improve the government’s ability to prevent, investigate and prosecute crimes affecting freight transportation companies and their drivers.
According to figures presented during the news conference on Wednesday by Mexican transportation publication T21 , Mexico recorded 6,211 cargo transportation robberies from January through September 2026.
CANACAR also reported 145 additional incidents during October.
Carlos García Álvarez, national president of HAMOTAC, expressed frustration that highway crimes have continued despite meetings with federal authorities.
Trucking groups identify 62 highways needing repairs
Infrastructure improvements represent another major component of the negotiations.
The trucking organizations submitted an assessment to Mexico’s Ministry of Infrastructure, Communications and Transportation (SICT) identifying 62 highway segments requiring priority maintenance and repairs.
The assessment is intended to help federal authorities identify roads for inclusion in future construction and maintenance programs.
Industry representatives also reported progress toward reclassifying approximately 11,000 kilometers, or 6,835 miles, of Mexico’s highway network.
The proposed changes cover 40 segments across 102 highways, with publication in Mexico’s Official Gazette expected by December.
Adalberto Gutiérrez Muñoz, national president of INDECO, criticized deteriorating highway conditions and the high tolls paid by commercial carriers.
He also called for improvements to highway access points that could be exploited by criminal organizations.
According to CANACAR, freight transportation companies contributed more than $3.6 billion, representing approximately 56% of toll highway revenue in 2025.
Government targets towing abuses and regulatory costs
Another significant agreement involves the planned December launch of SICT’s computerized towing service registration system, known as SIRSE.
The platform is designed to improve transparency in towing, vehicle recovery and impound services while reducing excessive charges and abusive practices.
Trucking representatives have repeatedly complained about towing costs and the difficulties associated with recovering commercial vehicles following accidents or law enforcement investigations.
The organizations also submitted an assessment of federal, state and municipal regulatory requirements to Mexico’s Digital Transformation and Telecommunications Agency.
The review could lead to a unified digital record for trucking companies and a single-window system intended to simplify administrative procedures.
Additional discussions include proposed tax incentives for private investment in secure truck parking facilities and driver rest areas.
Industry representatives are also seeking clarification of forthcoming labor regulations governing electronic work-hour records, including how driving, waiting, loading, unloading and rest periods will be classified.
MISUMI Americas expands Mexico operations with new 45,000-square-foot facility
MISUMI Americas has opened a new 45,000-square-foot manufacturing and fulfillment facility in Monterrey, Mexico , more than quadrupling its previous footprint as the company expands its capabilities to serve the country’s growing industrial sector.
The Oakland, California-based supplier of mechanical components and assemblies announced the expansion Nov. 16, saying the new facility adds in-house manufacturing and fulfillment of mechanical assemblies while strengthening its network of local manufacturing partners.
Since establishing its Mexico center of excellence in the Monterrey region in 2023, MISUMI Americas has expanded its Mexican manufacturing partner network by more than 250%, according to a news release.
The company’s Mexico operations support customers in aerospace, medical technology, semiconductors, robotics, automotive and energy. Its manufacturing capabilities include CNC machining, sheet metal fabrication, injection molding, extrusions and castings.
“Demand in Mexico has grown, and this facility is how we keep pace,” Dave Evans, president and CEO of MISUMI Americas, said in a statement. “Bringing assembly in-house and growing our manufacturing partner network gives customers more ways to get their parts and assemblies from one team.”
Prime Fuel Solutions expands Texas fleet, targets neighboring states
Abilene, Texas-based Prime Fuel Solutions is expanding its fuel delivery fleet and extending operations into neighboring states as it works toward establishing a nationwide fuel logistics network.
The company, which provides on-site fueling services for construction, industrial and other mission-critical projects, announced the expansion on Wednesday, along with the launch of a new website designed to streamline customer access to its services.
Prime Fuel Solutions said it is adding trucks and drivers to meet growing demand for scheduled and emergency fuel deliveries. The company provides diesel, gasoline, diesel exhaust fluid (DEF) and propane, along with bulk fuel storage, tank rentals and on-site fuel management.
Prime Fuel Solutions also offers 24-hour emergency fueling and delivery reporting. Its new website, primefuelsolutions.com , allows contractors to request quotes and access emergency fueling services.
The company, a sister business of Prime Equipment Solutions, serves construction, heavy civil, industrial and mission-critical projects.
The company did not disclose the number of vehicles added to its fleet, the investment involved or which neighboring states it plans to enter.
Why it matters: The negotiations could reduce cargo theft risks and costly disruptions along critical freight corridors connecting Mexican manufacturers with U.S. markets.

Ferrari Goes Old-School ICE Cool, Releases Twin 296 Challenge Stradale, Evo With 670+ HP Turbo Magic
74 photos
Photo: Ferrari
Just two days after GTA VI hit consoles, Maranello rolled out a pair of track-bred machines that look like they landed straight from the video game onto real asphalt. With towering fixed wings, aggressive front splitters, and stripped-back carbon-fiber bodywork, the 296 Challenge Stradale and 296 Challenge EVO pack the unmistakable visual punch of maxed-out Vice City supercars. The only difference is that neither needs a controller, an online lobby, or a cheat code to shred a real racetrack.
Ferrari unveiled the twins at the Finali Mondiali at the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya in Montmeló. Developed side by side, both cars pack a the three-liter, 120-degree twin-turbocharged V6 from the 296 GTB, but stripped of the hybrid bloatware. Both weigh 1.3 tons / 3,000 lb dry, and they represent Ferrari taking a big step back.
Not mechanically or technologically, but conceptually, putting grip and featherweight body mass ahead of electrification in both the road car and its track-only alter ego (Alter Evo?).
The 296 Challenge Stradale revives the nameplate last seen on the 360 Challenge Stradale in 2003, as Ferrari's most track-focused road car. Its mid-mounted, hot-V twin-turbo V6 produces 670 PS / 661 hp at 8,000 rpm and 740 Nm / 546 lb-ft of torque at 6,250 rpm with an 8,500 rpm redline. Revised boost control and variable valve timing lift dynamic torque by over 32% compared with the 296 GTB.
Photo: Ferrari Removing the battery and electric motor trims 140 kg / 309 lb compared with the 296 GTB, bringing dry weight to 1,330 kg / 2,932 lb. That yields a power-to-weight ratio of 497 bhp/metric ton. Race-derived hardware includes insulated turbochargers, Formula 1 knock-control software, a lighter flexplate, a Belt Starter Generator, and larger twin tailpipes, paired with an 8-speed dual-clutch gearbox mixing 296 Challenge logic with SF90 XX Stradale-derived 250-millisecond shifts.
Ferrari quotes 0 to 100 kph (62 mph), in 2.8 seconds, 0 to 200 kph/124 mph, in 7.9 seconds, and a top speed above 300 kph, or 186 mph. Braking from 200 kph takes 101 meters / 331 feet, and the checkered flag at Fiorano falls 1 minute and 18.5 seconds after start. Its fixed wing , splitter, flicks, aero damper, vortex generators, and enclosed underbody generate 617 kg / 1,360 lb of downforce at 250 kph (155 mph), up 72% from the standard 296 GTB.
Beneath the stripped-back bodywork, mechanical grip receives an equally serious upgrade. More aggressive suspension geometry works with adaptive dampers and springs over twice as stiff as previous road setups, paired with bespoke Pirelli P Zero R or P Zero Trofeo RS tires. ABS Evo operates across every Manettino mode and road condition, assisted by the F80 hypercar's Ferrari Integrated Vehicle Estimator to keep rear-wheel traction predictable when drivers push hard at the limit.
Photo: Ferrari Inside, the cabin discards everyday padding for tubular racing seats, technical fabrics, and single-piece carbon-fiber door panels stripped of armrests and storage pockets. Engineers also redesigned the center console and floor mats to shave further weight, while recalibrating the cabin sound system to balance intake and exhaust noise all the way to 8,500 rpm.
Despite that raw track-day specification, Ferrari still includes its standard 7-year maintenance program for every road-going buyer. For those who don’t like two-way lanes or traffic stops, the Evo is the alternative.
Built strictly for circuit competition, the 296 Challenge Evo is the tenth Challenge model in the Prancing Horse’s single-marque series established in 1993, debuting in the 2027 European and North American seasons. Its non-hybrid 3.0-liter V6 delivers 700 PS / 690 hp at 7,500 rpm, equaling 234 PS / 231 hp per liter, alongside 740 Nm / 546 lb-ft and an 8,500-rpm limit. With a seven-speed gearbox and the same 1,330 kg / 2,932 lb dry weight, it achieves 519 bhp/ton.
Photo: Ferrari Aerodynamics represent the biggest leap over the outgoing 296 Challenge, bringing the racer's balance closer to the 296 GT3 Evo. A reshaped underbody, revised splitter-to-floor transition, three pairs of front vortex generators, and two rear pairs lift peak downforce by 12%, adding roughly 100 kg / 220 lb at 250 kph/155 mph. Teams can switch between a High Downforce setup for technical circuits and a new Low Drag kit cutting minimum drag by 4%.
The aerodynamic load spread between those two configurations has more than doubled, letting engineers tailor balance across vastly different tracks. A wider rear-wing adjustment range, redesigned rear diffuser, revised mirrors, and added carbon-fiber components expand that setup window further. Raising rear ride height by up to 10 mm / 0.39 inches unlocks roughly 30 kg / 66 lb of extra downforce at 250 kph, while a cooled high-performance driveshaft handles sustained race loads.
Electronic updates target stability and cornering speed for both experienced amateur racers and younger circuit drivers. Reworked traction-control strategies and an upgraded electronic differential sharpen high-speed agility and braking poise across rapid direction changes. Carbon-ceramic CCM-R brakes work with a new pedal curve that increases modulation, travel, and pedal effort for the same deceleration.
Photo: Ferrari On the steering wheel, the Manettino provides four ABS calibrations tuned for dry or wet asphalt, balancing speed and stability.
In comparative track testing , the 296 Challenge Evo reduced tire wear and shaved 0.8 seconds per lap off the previous 296 Challenge at Mugello. A redesigned instrument cluster displays control intervention levels, tire-pressure data, and lap times more clearly during stints. Those upgrades prepare teams for the 2027 Ferrari Challenge calendar, which adds three 40-minute, two-driver endurance races featuring a mandatory pit stop, beginning with the season's second round at Mugello.

The Illinois Clean Ports Program is putting $104 million behind efforts to help clean up its working waterfronts, funds earmarked for heavy-duty electric equipment assets that includes forklifts, giant reach stackers, switcher locomotives, and the charging equipment needed to support them. There’s even a passenger ferry!
Procurement is now underway for zero-emission vehicles, equipment , and supporting infrastructure at four sites across the state. Administered by the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency (Illinois EPA), Illinois’ Clean Ports Program aims to modernize operations at ports and waterfront facilities in Chicago, the Quad Cities, and southern Illinois’ river port districts.
“Illinois’ waterways are a competitive advantage for the state,” said Illinois Governor JB Pritzker, who was elected to a historic third term on 03NOV. “By modernizing port infrastructure, advancing zero-emission technology, and improving air quality, we are strengthening our economy while building a cleaner future for Illinois.”
Holistic approach
Photo by Enel North America.
Illinois’ Clean Ports Program isn’t just replacing diesel-powered equipment with electric alternatives – instead, the plan also includes Level 2 and DC fast charging, shore power and charging for electrified ships , and comprehensive grid upgrades designed to modernize existing port operations and support the deployment of new electric equipment.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The program takes a holistic approach to port electrification at Chicago’s Illinois International Port District (IIPD), treating energy generation, storage, and deployment as parts of a single connected system. On-site solar helps meet the port’s growing electricity needs while excess power is stored for peak hours, when grid electricity is most expensive. This setup reduces strain on the local grid, and acts as a hedge against rising energy costs .
For smaller public port districts, replacing aging equipment and upgrading electrical infrastructure can be an enormous financial undertaking. The Illinois Clean Ports Program helps make those investments possible, bringing cleaner, healthier, zero-emission technology within reach of terminal operators while preparing the state’s ports for a more competitive freight future.

EICMA 2026 • Here Are Some of the Serious and Obscure Brands That EICMA 2026 Had To Offer – Worth Knowing About
1971 Dodge Super Bee Packs Numbers-Matching Hemi, One of Only 13 Made
21 photos
Photo: Mecum Auctions
Introduced for the 1968 model year, the Dodge Super Bee arrived in showrooms alongside the Plymouth Road Runner . Both were the entry-level muscle cars of their respective divisions. Although largely similar, the Mopar fared significantly differently on the market.
Plymouth hit a sales jackpot with the Road Runner, which moved a whopping 81,000 units in 1969. The Super Bee, however, reached its sales peak that same year at only 27,800 units. In 1971, when Chrysler discontinued its high-compression V8 engines, Plymouth had sold over 180,000 examples. Dodge, on the other hand, moved only 56,000 examples.
The vehicles also had different stints in showrooms. While the Super Bee was discontinued after the 1971 model year, the Road Runner soldiered on until 1975. The name remained in use until 1980 as a trim level on the compact Volare. All told, the Super Bee is the rarest of the pair, and the numbers become much lower when certain features are taken into account.
Unsurprisingly, the Super Bee becomes quite scarce when it rocks a 426-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) Hemi V8 engine. Records show that only 349 units were ordered with this powerplant. That's less than 1% of the Super Bee made between 1968 and 1971. Dodge sold most Hemi units in 1969, when 166 were ordered, while the final-year 1971 version is the rarest, with only 22 made. The blue coupe you see here is one of those holy-grail Mopars.
Muscle car sales were at an all-time low in 1971. With new emission ratings just around the corner and with performance cars quite expensive to insure, drivers were starting to lose interest in beefed-up rigs. The Super Bee was favored by only 5,054 customers that year, which likely sealed its fate.
Most of these cars were ordered with the standard 383-cubic-inch (6.3-liter) V8; that's 3,858 units. Exactly 307 customers went with the 340-cubic-inch (5.6-liter) small-block, while 26 picked the 440-cubic-inch (7.2-liter) RB. Finally, Dodge sold 99 units with the 440 Six-Pack and the 22 cars equipped with the Hemi that I mentioned earlier.
Of these, 13 were fitted with the three-speed TorqueFlite automatic, while the remaining eight examples got the four-speed manual gearbox. These cars rarely pop for sale, which is why this Super Bee's appearance among the lots of Mecum's Kissimmee 2027 auction is a big deal.
Scheduled to go under the hammer on January 14, this Hemi Super Bee is one of those 13 cars equipped with the TorqueFlite automatic. The Mopar still has the numbers-matching drivetrain, and the ad also mentions an "original interior" and "original factory sheet metal." It's not described as a survivor, so it's safe to assume that it was repainted at some point.
The engine was also rebuilt, with the seller having spent an estimated $30,000 to bring it back to Concours-ready condition. The original carburetors have been restored. The unit was refreshed by Harms Automotive.
This Super Bee is one of fewer than 10 Hemi units that popped up at public auctions in recent years. As far as I know, only six cars have been auctioned off publicly since 2010, and only three changed ownership (the other units remained unsold due to higher reserves).
As of this writing, the most expensive 1971 Hemi Super Bee is a Light Gunmetal example that fetched $269,500 in 2024. Two more examples sold for $209,000 each in 2023 and 2015. The record car has a four-speed manual, with one of the $209K units sporting an automatic.
This B7 Blue example will also fetch a six-figure sum, and I wouldn't be surprised to see it setting a new record. If anything, it should at least become the world's most expensive automatic car. How much do you think this Super Bee is worth?

Tuner Drops New Body Kit for the Old F80 BMW M3
11 photos
Photo: Instagram | revozportt
Just because you own an older generation of the BMW M3 does not mean that you cannot make it more special, because there are numerous aftermarket upgrades available for it, and some of them have been signed by renowned tuners.
In this case, we are talking about RevoZport, which recently took to its social media channels to release these pictures, which depict a modded F80 M3. Mind you, that’s the older model, which was made from 2014 to 2018, and was offered strictly as a four-door sedan, with pure rear-wheel drive, and a 3-liter twin-turbo straight-six paired either with a six-speed manual or a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission.
Speaking of the mill, you should know that it produced 425 hp (317 kW /431 ps) and 406 lb-ft (550 Nm) of torque. That’s not bad at all, even by today’s standards, and the same can be said about the performance numbers, too. With 4.1 seconds needed to hit 62 mph (100 kph) from a standstill, this generation of the BMW M3 was pretty much as fast as today’s base M3. The top speed was electronically limited to 155 mph (250 kph).
Photo: Instagram | revozportt Now, the pictured F80 BMW M3 is not about more oomph, but enhanced looks. We can see that the hood is new, and so is the splitter, as well as the add-ons surrounding the side vents in the front bumper. There is new trim on the front fenders, too, and new side skirt attachments are also on deck. The changes continue at the rear, where this car has a massive wing attached to the trunk lid, as well as a new skirt.
The BMW roundels and the M logos are still visible, and that’s a nice touch if you ask me, and in this case, the German sports sedan features a blue look, numerous black details, and tinted windows. This Audi RS3 Sportback Is a 630-Horsepower Mega Hatch
10 photos
Photo: Instagram | abt_sportsline
If you remember ABT’s RS3 630 that we covered a couple of months ago, then you know that it is one of the coolest mega hatches out there. After all, do you know of any other similar ride to boast this much oomph and still look almost stock?
Speaking of the oomph, it is rated at 630 horsepower. That’s metric horsepower, by the way, because this thing lives on the right side of the Atlantic Ocean. This translates to 621 bhp and 463 kW, and the thrust is said to be rated at 516 pound-feet (700 Nm).
By comparison, the standard Audi RS 3 Sportback comes with 394 bhp (400 ps/294 kW) and 369 lb-ft (500 Nm) of torque with no outside intervention. The 2.5-liter turbocharged five-cylinder unit enables 0-62 mph (0-100 kph) in 3.8 seconds, with a top speed of 155 mph (250 kph) or up to 190 mph (290 kph).
We have no idea how fast the ABT RS3 630 is, because ABT Sportsline hasn’t mentioned this aspect. However, their RS3-R build, which came with 503 bhp (510 ps/375 kW) and 443 pound-feet (600 Nm) of torque, is said to have completed the sprint in 3.3 seconds. As a result, we can assume that the RS3 630 is perhaps a couple of tenths of a second faster.
Photo: Instagram | abt_sportsline But why revisit this particular project when we already dedicated a story to it? For the simple reason that the one pictured in the gallery is new. The tuner says that its paint finish is called the Ipanema (just like the famous beach in Rio de Janeiro, Brasil) Brown Metallic, joined by plenty of black elements, and a set of gold-finished wheels.
The car in question also features new skirts on the lower parts of the body, has ABT logos at the front and rear, and on the new alloys, as well as some ABT touches on the inside, which are partially visible in these new pictures. The previous ABT RS3 630 that we covered also featured the tuner’s anniversary logo on the central armrest, special floor mats, and a few other things.
ABT Sportsline has limited the RS3 630’s production to 30 units worldwide. We still do not know how many of them are available, but the one pictured above, with its Ipanema Brown Metallic color and gold wheels, as well as some extras inside and out, and a healthy power boost, is searching for a new home as we speak. And if you want to make it yours, then you should reach out to the tuner to discuss additional details.
Now, would you ever see yourself driving an Audi RS 3 Sportback that has more power than some of yesterday’s supercars? I definitely wouldn’t mind it, and for what it’s worth, I think that the ABT RS3 630 is a great build. View this post on Instagram A post shared by ABT Sportsline (@abt_sportsline)

EICMA 2026 • 2026 EICMA's Speed Legends Exhibit Was Not To Be Missed – See the Bikes That Paved MotoGP History
Owner Takes His Cadillac Escalade-V to a Tuner, Goes Home With 800 Horsepower
10 photos
Photo: Late Model Racecraft | YouTube
For some car owners out there, stock just doesn’t cut it. They need to go beyond the factory standard. That's exactly what the owner of this Cadillac Escalade wanted. One day, he took his full-size SUV to a tuner in Texas to surprise his wife. A couple of weeks later, he drove home in an 800-horsepower monster with good road manners and oomph enough to make other drivers at the stoplight wonder.
Scott was the one who brought in his wife's Cadillac Escalade all the way from Connecticut. This build is actually an early Christmas gift for his wife, Lauren. He bought it sight unseen and took it straight to a tuner in Katy, Texas, to have it transformed.
Finished in Argent Silver Metallic, an $825 option, the Escalade wears one of the rarest colors since most of them are sold in either black or white. However, the family plans to have it wrapped. It will happen when the missus chooses the color.
The Cadillac Escalade-V is a monster from the moment it rolls off the production line of the General Motors Arlington Assembly Plant in Arlington, Texas. It comes with the 6.2-liter supercharged V8, pumping out a massive 682 horsepower (691 metric horsepower) and 653 pound-feet (885 Newton meters) of torque.
Photo: Late Model Racecraft | YouTube That is enough for the SUV to rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in just 4.4 seconds, despite playing in the heavyweight category at 6,217 pounds (2,820 kilograms), on its way to a top speed of 125 mph (201 kph).
However, all those figures are far behind. When it entered the shop, the Escalade-V baselined at 500 rear-wheel horsepower and 477 pound-feet of rear-wheel torque. Now, it is driving off with 644 rear-wheel horsepower, which translates to roughly 800 at the crank, and 587 pound-feet of torque. Late Model Racecraft ’s 800 HP Package is to blame for the extra oomph.
The Escalade-V got a larger throttle body, a custom elbow, an S&B cold air induction system, and a tuned ECM, but it retains the stock supercharger, fully ported and getting more airflow. Also factory are the headers, manifolds, and exhaust. This makes it still idle and drive like it did the day it left the factory, but with a solid horsepower gain.
Lauren won't even know the difference until she steps on it. Now, in V Mode, her brand-newCadillac Escalade-V acts and sounds like a Chevy Corvette. She is definitely going to notice that!
Photo: Late Model Racecraft | YouTube Steven Fereday takes the SUV for a spin to make sure he is delivering a reliable vehicle and is sure that Scott will probably drive it more than his missus. Each acceleration puts a smile on his face. It is probably going to have the same effect on Lauren and Scott.
Scott jumped into the comments section to tell LMR that he will ship his C6 Chevy Corvette ZR1 to them for an upgrade.

Developed by Japanese material handling giant Tadano, the 35-ton V320RC wheeled electric pick & carry crane has spent the last few months proving itself at NMG Italia’s job sites, where it’s been handling heavy loads in tight industrial spaces and improving efficiency by 50%. And now, you can buy one.
Developed in collaboration with NMG Italia, the V320RC electric crane has already proven its performance in the field with NMG and during precision setup operations at Marmomac, a trade show dedicated to the marble industry held each year in Verona.
“The ( Tadano ) V320RC marks a real breakthrough in the pick & carry industry,” reads the official Tadano launch copy. “ Rather than an evolution of existing solutions , it introduces a new philosophy, with technologies and features capable of setting new benchmarks in the lifting market. Tadano and NMG Italia continue their collaboration in the field, turning real-world experience into new technological solutions to meet the most advanced demands of industrial lifting.”
The crane itself is a compact, battery-electric pick-and-carry machine with a maximum lifting capacity of 35 tonnes. Measuring just 5 m long, 2.15 m wide and 2.400 m tall (a meter is about a yard, guys – you got this), the V320RC is designed to bring heavy lifting capability into tight industrial spaces where larger cranes struggle to operate.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The new Tadano runs on a 120V, 1,120 Ah li-ion battery pack (that works out to ~134 kWh) and packs a gross vehicle weight of more than 31,150 kg (~34.5 short tones). That number includes 9,500 kg (~10 tons) of removable counterweights that make transport and handling easier for a wider range of customers. Under the hood, a new hydraulic system pairs a variable-displacement pump with what the company calls “an electro-hydraulic control valve” to improve precision and responsiveness while reducing energy consumption.
According to NMG Italia, all that baked-in tech V320RC give them 50% better productivity than competing electric cranes working under equivalent workloads, with enough battery capacity to support several days of operation between charges .

Virtual BMW X9 Doesn't Care About the Mercedes GLS or Audi Q7, Instead Targets Q9 and Caddy Escalade
14 photos
Photo: carlchan100 / Instagram
The premium Bavarian automaker BMW has prepared a ton of new stuff going into 2027 – but we’re not sure that a flagship crossover SUV larger than the current X7 is also on the menu. But the parallel universes of vehicular CGI seem to think so.
The global luxury crown belongs to BMW, and you can’t hold on to the throne without breaking a sweat – BMW has been on top of the charts above Mercedes-Benz since 2021 and has no intention of vacating the premises. As such, it’s no wonder that a lot of novelties are coming next year.
The list includes a new entry-level EV , the potential BMW i1 hatchback with a short rear and Neue Klasse attire; the reworked X1 and iX1 base crossover SUVs; minor updates for the X2 and iX2 crossover coupe-SUVs; the station wagon version of the new electric 3 Series; the M3 and the first all-electric M3 ; an X3 M with electricity along with an iX4 M; the mid-cycle refresh of the 5 Series; and the switch to electricity of the iX7 plus the new BMW Alpina 7 Series as a rival for Maybach.
It’s pretty hard to also cram a flagship BMW X9 in there in the real world, so leave it to the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI to fill in the blanks. For example, Carl Chan, an MA in Intelligent Mobility from the Royal College of Art in London, the UK, is also known as ' carlchan100 ' on social media because of things like this unofficial, hypothetical design project.
His vision of the BMW X9 ultra-luxury full-size three-row crossover SUV is pretty simple and mindful – a combination of the current BMW X7’s split headlights and a large kidney grille with elements taken from the Neue Klasse but adapted for a more elegant posture. The SUV is also pretty muscular, with a massive shoulder line to give it the look of a widebody model, especially above the rear fenders.
Around the back, the Neue Klasse LED taillights are more than obvious, along with a sculpted bumper to add precious inches to the crumple zones. There’s also a full-length panoramic glass roof, but even so we can’t see inside the cockpit because there’s no accompanying rendering from the pixel master. So, what do you think – cool or not?
As for the rumor mill, the latest reports on the whereabouts of the potential BMW X9 discuss about a combination of the Neue Klasse design and the enhanced CLAR architecture to allow for the massive SUV built in America to include powerful gasoline engines and satisfy the current adversity for EVs. So, is this a good rival for the Audi Q9 and the Cadillac Escalade? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Carl Chan (@carlchan100)

Second-Gen Polestar 2 Gets Unofficially Imagined Based on Formula 2030 Concept, Lacks a Rear Window
8 photos
Photo: sugardesign_1 / Instagram
Polestar Automotive Holding UK PLC, known simply as Polestar , is the premium sports Swedish automotive manufacturer crafted as the brainchild of both Volvo Cars and its Chinese parent company Geely.
Polestar, which is traded publicly on the Nasdaq stock exchange, is headquartered in Gothenburg, Sweden, and mainly sells automobiles across North America, Europe, and the Asia Pacific regions. It was established as an independent brand in 2017, and the first model they created was dubbed simply Polestar 1, a plug-in hybrid grand tourer made in China in just 1,500 units.
Currently, the roster is composed of Polestar 2 , 3, 4 as a coupe or SUV, and the Polestar 5. There will be many new introductions in the near future: the Polestar 2’s fresh successor will launch next year, followed by the Polestar 7 compact SUV coming in 2028, and the Polestar 6 roadster as a hero model further down the line.
The first-generation Polestar 2 was the company’s first mass-produced model, and earlier this month ended production after more than 200k units – the brand’s Tesla Model 3 rival will get a successor in 2027, most likely continuing its legacy as a five-door liftback sedan proposition.
Recently, Polestar unveiled a fancy prototype dubbed the Polestar Formula 2030 Concept, a model that looks like a hot hatchback or something that Saab would create if they were still around, and comes with coach rear doors to make it worth our attention.
However, the company says it won’t be produced, and instead various styling elements will make their way to the new models it has cooking, like the next-gen Polestar 2 and a future Polestar 7 model. Well, if you can’t wait to see the Formula 2030 translated into a more serious model, the parallel universes of vehicular CGI will come to your aid via the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators.
More precisely, Sugar Chow, the virtual artist better known as " sugardesign_1 " on social media, has decided to CGI-present his vision for the all-new, second-gen Polestar 2 liftback – and it’s fully inspired by the Formula 2030, quite obviously.
The pixel master adapts the concept’s design features into a series-production model, keeping the split headlights and DRLs along with the fresh bumper style. But the profile is of a classic liftback now, and while the rear reuses the concept’s slim LED taillights and the bumper with cutouts and integrated diffuser, it’s also wackier now because it lacks a standard rear window.
Naturally, the all-new Polestar 2 would continue as an electric-only model, this time around produced on a dedicated EV platform that’s not shared with combustion models. So, what do you think – yay or nay for this unofficial, hypothetical design project? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sugarchow (@sugardesign_1)

Things Are Finally Looking Up for "Luminosity" Megayacht After Years of Abandonment and Neglect
52 photos
Photo: Benetti Yachts
The yachting industry's most celebrated and stellar build is, ironically so, one that wider audiences have heard little about, let alone see out there in all the popular spots where superyachts tend to congregate. Even worse, it's been spending the past four years in neglect and abandonment, piling on debt and damages.
Luminosity is that build: a megayacht by length and volume, a gigayacht by innovation and amenities, and a one-off in terms of how it blends technology and art to create the ultimate tribute to beauty. Luminosity is a multiple world record holder across various categories, including the world's largest hybrid vessel and the only one to feature an almost full glass superstructure.
Sadly, it's not these records that have turned it into a regular fixture in the media, but its current condition. Luminosity was delivered without an owner in 2020, was eventually bought in 2022, but before the new owner could take it out on its maiden journey, it was seized and frozen in Montenegro.
For the past four years, Luminosity has been frozen in place , with a crew so small onboard that not even the bare minimum of maintenance is being carried out, accruing debt and damages. And for the first time in four years, things are looking up: a new report says that a verbal agreement has been reached for its sale, with the interested party fully aware of the vessel's debts and condition.
Photo: Benetti Yachts A ray of hope Luminosity has been docked in Montenegro for all this time, with just about 5 or 6 people onboard carrying out whatever they can in terms of maintenance, which is very little if you consider its size. It was listed for the first time in the summer of 2024, with an asking of "just" €135 million (approximately $148 million at the current exchange rate) – a steal for its reported value of $270 million.
The Yacht Report notes that progress has been recorded in recent weeks, but that it has passed under the radar because nothing is official yet. The original report is included in the first video embedded below, starting at the 16.02-minute mark.
Photo: Benetti Yachts It notes that Monaco-based yacht broker Russell Crump has informed the union that a verbal offer "has been accepted to purchase the vessel" and that sanctions and asset recovery lawyer Martin de Luca is representing the owners. The verbal offer is "pending final terms and documentation," but the buyer is fully aware of the outstanding debt and issues with the vessel, and that they will have to be settled before the deed changes hands.
In addition to the damages caused by improper maintenance , which are believed to be considerable after all this time of neglect, Luminosity is also behind with crew salaries. The new owner will have to pick the tab on all this, before they're even able to take the vessel into drydock.
The same report says that another prospective buyer has emerged, with the implication that, even if this deal falls through despite the promising start, not all is lost.
Photo: Benetti Yachts A star that never got the chance to shine Luminosity was commissioned by Kuwaiti billionaire Kutayba Yusuf Ahmed Alghanim, who reportedly approached Benetti Yachts with a very specific request, namely that he wanted a megayacht with an entire superstructure of glass. His demands continue to change, pushing back the delivery timeline as the yard tried to accommodate them.
Weeks before delivery, the billionaire bailed, citing the same delays as the grounds for his refusal to accept delivery. Benetti launched the vessel without an owner, and it would take another two years before one would come along, in an off-the-market deal.
Photo: Benetti Yachts The second one would prove even worse luck than the first. Russian oligarch Andrey Guryev bought Luminosity right before the sweeping wave of international sanctions, which eventually included his name, so his assets, like Luminosity and the equally famous Alfa Nero , would be seized.
Alfa Nero has moved on to greener pastures after a while, but Luminosity is still stuck in limbo.
It shouldn't come as a surprise that all this controversy is shining the wrong spotlight on Luminosity, which remains nonetheless one of the most beautiful and innovative builds of modern times.
Photo: Benetti Yachts Built on a naval architecture by Benetti and with interiors by Zaniz Interiors, Luminosity has a total length of 353 feet (107 meters) and an interior volume of 5,884 GT spread across six decks connected by a sculptural floating staircase and an all-glass elevator. It offers accommodation for as many as 24 guests in 12 suites and 37 crew, and is able to redefine interior design through its all-glass superstructure.
Amenities include a certified helideck with a fueling station, a beach club spa area that integrates everything from a gym and wellness area to an indoor pool and a sauna, a Moon Lounge that offers alfresco dining and entertainment and doubles as a second master suite for a VIP guest because it has its own suite attached, and curated art and technology pieces throughout.
Benetti says it was "conceived to evoke the idea of a moving palace of glass and with an artistic soul," which is quite accurate but also slightly ironic in the bigger context of it never having sailed on its maiden journey.
Photo: Benetti Yachts The actual master suite takes up an entire deck and offers a massage room, a private pantry, an outdoor terrace, his and hers offices, a master bathroom with a statement jacuzzi tub carved out of a single piece of Carrara marble, and the lowest level of noise and vibration on the ship, equivalent to what you'll find in a hushed library.
Benetti maintains that all this luxury is second to the true crown jewel, which is this gigantic vessel's ability to sail with reduced emissions and noiselessly in certain condition. Luminosity is the largest hybrid vessel around, with a state-of-the-art system that combines two 2,200kW electric azipods, six 1,000kW diesel generators, and a three megawatt battery bank.
Photo: Benetti Yachts Luminosity can run house functions at anchor on batteries alone for 24 hours and can cruise into protected waters without an issue. At full throttle, it will hit 16.5 knots (19 mph/30.5 kph), with range at cruising speed being 8,000+ nautical miles (9,206 miles/14,816 km).
Via // The Yacht Report on YouTube

Release Layer System: The Future of Motorcycle Helmet Safety Is Here
26 photos
Photo: AGV
Have you ever heard someone say : “I would love to ride a motorcycle, but my wife won’t let me do it because it’s too dangerous.”? I think I’ve met three different people this year alone who were facing that sort of situation. And there are several ways to interpret it all.
I consider myself lucky for having met my wife at the racetrack, just before my qualifying session on a BMW G310R. I suffered a lowside later that day, which meant I fractured my jaw and lost several teeth, all because the helmet size wasn’t correct. Still, my wife has never told me I should stop riding bikes, although she is obviously concerned whenever I go out. So, I guess I can understand the wives that are completely against motorcycles in their families.
Raising a kid takes a dad and a mom, after all. Fear is a driving factor in that position, and I guess you can look at it from another perspective: maybe it’s the husband who’s too afraid to overcome that fear of crashing, and he’s just using his wife as an excuse. If you were mean about it, you could say he just “chickened out”, but ultimately everyone is free to live his own life as he wishes. And let’s face it, riding a motorcycle is just not as safe as driving a car.
I’ve tried my best to advise my friends and acquaintances to take things slowly and use proper riding gear every time they go out. And yet, some of them will still try to buy the cheapest helmet possible, or even worse: a used one which they know nothing about. I guess ignorance really is bliss. If you don’t even realize what could happen to your brain in case of an accident, there’s no fear involved, so there’s nothing to worry about.
Sadly, the laws of physics are still in effect whether you’re aware of them or not. “All the gear, all the time” should be your mantra if you enjoy riding motorcycles, and especially so if you’ve got someone waiting for you at home. Everything I’ve said so far should sum up why I was so excited to discover AGV’s new Pista GP R3 helmet featuring RLS technology .
I witnessed a horrendous accident Photo: RLS It debuted at the San Marino Grand Prix, showcasing a new Release Layer System that seems very much like a huge step forward for rider safety by making the risk of a concussion occurring six times less likely than before. I immediately remember something Peter from Family Guy said: “Why are we not funding this?”
Anyway, I wanted to learn more about this new tech and the people who are working on it, and that’s how I managed to chat to James Cook, who is the founder of UK-based RLS, which ranked #1 in Virginia Tech's helmet safety testing since launching in cycling. Many years ago, while James was riding his bicycle , he witnessed a horrendous accident that would compel him to find a way to reduce the risks associated with bicycles and motorcycles alike.
“I was doing my engineering degree, trying to find a way to improve helmet safety, I used 3D printing to create a new custom fit helmet. I was really motivated to try and find a way to push things forward.” One of the things that shocked me while reading the the RLS white paper was an analysis by Baker et al. 2026 which explained how 25 years of helmet and vehicle design have reduced the prevalence of head injury without resolving the problem.
An analysis of 353 motorcyclists from collisions in the UK between 2013 to 2025 revealed that a third of them suffered head injuries, while a quarter of them had a clinically classified traumatic brain injury. Yikes! I was curious to learn more about the people who are working alongside James to bring RLS technology into our lives. “We have two people with a PHD in bio-mechanics. They focus on creating test rigs, working with test standards understanding how helmet safety relates to brain injury.”
This is not a high-speed racing problem Photo: RLS “We also have someone on the team who used to work for MIPS and Bell . Most of the other members are engineers. We really see the technology as a platform that can work across different helmets (bicycle, motorcycle, snow etc).” I wasn’t too bad at anatomy class in school, but learning about how accidents affect the human body was never part of the program. That’s not to say I didn’t realize that crashes could affect your brain, especially since I dedicated many years of my life to skateboarding.
Still, falling of a bicycle or motorcycle and hitting something means your head can rotate sharply. “Brain inside the skull lags, twists, and the tissue is stretched. Nerve fibers (axons) running through the whole volume can be strained at once. COST 327 had to analyze concussion separately from every other brain injury in its database since its location and occurrence were difficult to identify, yet it was prevalent and happened at speeds riders would consider ordinary.”
“The median head impact speed at which concussion occurred was 43 km/h, so this is not just a high-speed racing problem. COST 327 concluded that, for head injuries of AIS 2 or greater, rotational motion was the cause of over 60% of the injuries, with linear motion accounting for around 30%.” You can say what you want about 2026: that life has become more expensive, that there are too many conflicts going on, that cars and bikes aren’t as exciting as they were in the ‘90s and the list goes on.
But it’s so reassuring to know that some people are still working hard at bringing important tech into our lives, helping us enjoy the things that we love while reducing the risks involved. The current information obtained by researchers clearly shows that safety standards should focus on both linear shock absorption and rotational energy deflection, something both the ECE R22.06 and FIM FRHPhe-02 (required for professional circuit racing) ratings have been evaluating recently.
The future is now! Photo: RLS “Whereas MIPS tech involved using a low-friction slip layer inside the helmet, RLS features an array of 2 mm polycarbonate spheres bonded to the helmet's outer shell and covered by an additional outer panel. The panel’s fasteners and adhesive bonds sever on an an oblique impact freeing the spheres to roll and the panel to flex away from the main helmet shell.”
“This release mechanism disperses and transforms a substantial share of the impact's rotational energy before it reaches the head, complementing the EPS liner's absorption of the remaining linear force” . It all sounds simple enough, but it has proven to be effective according to tests performed in the FIM lab. With the system on the helmet, the risk of moderate-to-severe brain injury was reduced from 48% to 1% on frontal upper face impacts (0 degrees) and from 32% to 7% for side impacts (270 degrees).
James couldn’t tell me all about the company’s plans for the near future, but I believe every single helmet brand on the market will either try to work with him for their next products or develop their own, similar solution to the rotational energy problem. That’s a huge win for anyone who rides bicycles or motorcycles, and I believe it could very well expand into karting and F1, too.
Since AGV chose to work with RLS on their helmets , I take that as a clear sign that this technology is going to push the industry standards forward. The question is, how long until the DOT and ECE ratings will adjust to be on the same level with the FIM2 protocol? With any luck, I might get to test the AGV Pista GP R3 next year, and maybe even tour the RLS headquarters for a deeper dive into the tests and plans for the next five to 10 years.

All-New Toyota Corolla Cross Jumps From Behind the CGI Curtain, Also Gets Compared to Current One
6 photos
Photo: kelsonik / Instagram
The Japanese automaker has a lot of interesting things going around – from the speculation regarding the GR Celica to the new Scion Kei-01 truck that costs less than a Ford Maverick and is going to be available in America soon.
While average new prices reach new heights – they crossed the $51k threshold back in October in the United States, Toyota is fighting against the trend with a revival of the Scion moniker for a four-wheel drive kei truck built in the US . The catch is that it’s limited to 25 mph, so it won’t bring you too many bragging rights, even though it might be cheaper than a Ford Maverick.
The company is also playing with the hearts of sports car enthusiasts because it’s unwilling to say whether or not a GR Celica revival is also coming to the streets after it has only confirmed the nameplate’s return for the 2027 WRC season. In other news, Toyota recently launched the new Corolla Deck model for the Latin American and Caribbean regions.
It’s a very interesting model – the often-reported unibody compact pickup truck is now live, complete with hybrid power, though it’s not coming to North America to fight the aforementioned Ford Maverick. But while we’re on the subject of the Toyota Corolla Cross, let’s just say that it’s a very dear model to many folks – including the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI.
For example, Nikita Chuicko, the virtual artist better known as " kelsonik " on social media, thinks that now is the right CGI time to work on the compact crossover SUV that launched based on the same TNGA-C platform as the E210 series Corolla during the summer of 2020. Now, following a recent mid-cycle refresh procedure also available in North America and the recent Corolla Deck launch for other regions, the pixel master thinks it’s time to start work on the second generation.
His unofficial, hypothetical design project is further speculation upon the Toyota Corolla Concept presented at the Japan Mobility Show in 2025. Now, everyone and their dog expects the Japanese automaker to reveal the 13th generation of the Corolla series sometime next year for the 2028MY, with influences taken directly from the multi-energy prototype.
Further extrapolating, the CGI expert now unifies the design of the regular, upcoming Corolla passenger car with the Corolla Cross, deploying the new front style combined with a dual-tone paintjob and the high-riding compact crossover SUV profile. This model is also all-electric or a plug-in hybrid, as it has a front charging port located next to the driver’s door.
Last but not least, we also have a quick comparison between the current SUV and the new CGI one. So, what do you think – yay or nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by CAR DESIGN | RENDERINGS (@kelsonik)
